## TabStation 2.18.17

**Windows Quick Settings**
- The Wi-Fi and Bluetooth buttons are split like Windows 11. Tap the left side to turn them on or off, or tap the arrow (>) to see a list in the same panel. The name of the connected network or device shows under each button.
- The Wi-Fi list shows the connected network, then saved networks, then other networks nearby by signal strength. Tap an open network to join it. A secured network opens the system Wi-Fi panel for the password.
- The Bluetooth list shows connected and paired devices, then searches for nearby devices. Tap a nearby device to pair it.
- New buttons: Lock screen, Mobile hotspot, Airplane mode, Battery saver, Dark mode, Silent and Location. They replace the Settings and Power buttons. You can still shut down from the Start menu. Touch and hold Mobile hotspot to open its settings.
- Buttons come in pages of six. Swipe or flick up or down, scroll with a mouse or touchpad, or tap the arrows next to the dots.
- Choose where sound plays: tap the speaker button next to the volume slider to pick the tablet speaker, Bluetooth, wired or USB headphones, or HDMI. Requires Shizuku.
- Every button switches instantly, without a pause or a flash. Lock screen turns the screen off almost immediately.

**macOS Control Center**
- Tap the Display card for brightness, Dark Mode, Reading Mode and Auto-Brightness. Tap the Sound card to switch between sound outputs.
- Tap Now Playing for a wide Now Playing menu with the cover, title, artist, controls and a progress bar you can drag. Tap the cover to open the app that's playing.
- Tap the title of a menu opened from Control Center to go back to Control Center.
- The Focus card has an arrow (>) for the Focus menu. Tap the rest of the card to turn Do Not Disturb on or off.
- Tap the icons at either end of the Display and Sound sliders to change brightness or volume a step.
- Do Not Disturb, Rotation and Dark Mode change instantly, and Control Center stays open. The round buttons are bigger and sit closer together.

**Notifications**
- While TabStation is on, notification pop-ups come from TabStation instead of HyperOS: a frosted banner in macOS mode, a toast above the taskbar in Windows mode. Tap to open, use its buttons, or swipe right or tap ✕ to close. HyperOS pop-ups come back when you turn TabStation off. You can switch this off in Settings → Style & controls.

**Everywhere**
- App icons in the Dock, taskbar, Launchpad and Start menu shrink a little when you press them and bounce back when you let go.
- The macOS menu bar battery looks like macOS 26: green while charging, yellow with battery saver, red at 20% or less.
- A menu bar icon stays highlighted while its menu is open.
- Battery saver is dimmed while the tablet charges, because Android doesn't allow turning it on then.
- Launchpad no longer closes while you scroll. To close it with a swipe, keep pulling past the top or bottom of the list.
- Opening an app that wasn't running looks smoother, without a dark flash at the end of the loading screen.
- The Shut down and Lock icons in the Windows Start menu no longer show as empty boxes.
- Fixed a notification banner that could stay on screen, and a few other small bugs.
- TabStation uses a little less CPU while idle.

Requires Android 10+. Shizuku is recommended. Install over the previous version; settings are kept. TabStation updates itself from Settings → Version & updates.

## TabStation 2.18.16

- The app switcher opens with Alt + 1 (or Alt + `). Keep holding Alt and press 1 again to move to the next app, add Shift to go back, then let go of Alt to switch. Alt + Esc no longer opens it, because apps treat Esc as Back and closed themselves. Alt + Tab stays with HyperOS Recents.
- Choosing an app that is already open in the switcher now only brings it to the front. It no longer plays the opening animation, and the window keeps its size and position instead of turning full screen or minimizing.
- The switcher opens instantly and only lists apps that are still open. An app you just closed no longer shows up, so choosing it can't reopen it with a loading screen.
- Opening Control Center no longer takes over the Dolby effect from the system sound settings. TabStation only takes over when you tap the Dolby button.

Requires Android 10+. Shizuku is recommended. Install over the previous version; settings are kept. TabStation updates itself from Settings → Version & updates.

## TabStation 2.18.15

- Fixed apps turning black after you open them from a notification or tap the ⋯ handle at the top of the screen. TabStation could reopen its desktop while HyperOS was still animating, which left the app invisible and sometimes made it show "isn't responding". TabStation now waits until HyperOS has finished.
- New Control Center in Liquid Glass style, laid out like macOS: each control floats on its own frosted-glass tile with real blur behind it. Wi-Fi shows the network name, and there is a Now Playing tile with play, pause and skip, plus Rotation, Screenshot, Show Desktop, Dark Mode, Battery Saver, Focus, Display and Sound.
- Dolby Atmos on/off in Control Center (the "Dolby" button on the Sound card) and in the Sound menu. Touch and hold to open the Dolby settings.
- Notification Center, the Dock, the menu bar, menus, Spotlight, the app switcher and the Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Sound and Focus menus now use the same frosted glass.
- Notification stacks work like macOS: tap a stack to unfold it in place, and "Show less" folds it again, both animated. Notifications are a bit smaller and closer together, and the Notification Center title is smaller.
- Turning Wi-Fi or Bluetooth on or off in their menus no longer reloads the menu. The list grows or shrinks smoothly and the devices fade in.
- The app switcher now opens with Alt + Esc too, for keyboards where Esc and ` share one key. Keep holding Alt and press Esc again to move to the next app, then let go of Alt to switch. It lists all open apps, most recent first. When no apps are open, it lists the apps you used last. The icons are centered, and the app's name sits under the selected icon.
- Pressing the Windows/Command key (the square key next to Alt) on its own opens Launchpad. TabStation hides the HyperOS dock that the key also brings up.
- The Glass opacity setting now applies to everything in macOS mode: the Dock, menu bar, panels, menus, Spotlight and widgets.
- Clearer toggles (from 2.18.14).

Requires Android 10+. Shizuku is recommended. Install over the previous version; settings are kept. TabStation updates itself from Settings → Version & updates.
